transcript: Did you know they opened a Spirit Halloween in the bones of an abandoned Broadway theatre? Let's talk about the “secret” abandoned Broadway theatres hidden in plain sight. Maybe the one people see the most but rarely noticed is the lobby of the Times Square AMC. Here you can see the prescenium arch and the boxes on the side. There's the mezzanine and the balcony. And this used to be at the Empire Theater, which, of course, is the namesake for the current AMC, Empire 25. Somewhat less covert is the former Mark Hellinger Theater, which now operates as the Times Square Church. This is the one that people bring up maybe most frequently when they speculate about adding another Broadway theater. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I believe I've heard before that the situation is just as simple as the Times Square Church operates it and they don't wanna give it up. But there's another abandoned Broadway theater hidden behind these doors. The entrance is in this lobby on 42nd Street, where you also go into the Dave and Buster's and the Applebee's and where you exit from the AMC. And it says Liberty Diner, because actually, there used to be a diner there. And the theater was the Liberty Theater. Even after the diner closed, It's been used in a variety of ways over the years, from events to immersive theater and maybe most comically, like I said at the beginning, it spent a couple seasons as a Spirit Halloween, which was actually when I was able to go see it. You can see in this photo those are the costume racks, but I think they stopped doing that in maybe 2019. And I don't know that it's been open to the public since. There were rumors of things they were planning to do with it, but nothing that's come to fruition. And so currently, I believe you cannot go inside this one, but you can see the back of it from 41st Street. I've heard a few different explanations over the years about why this hasn't or won't be converted back into a Broadway theatre. From, like, fire code, spacing and logistics, desirability of the space. I don't know which one is accurate, but it does seem clear that the owners have no interest in that path.
